chapter: Armstrong, Parker and life inside the Basie band
title: Ten years with Basie and how the band changed
summary: Tate was in the band 1939 to about 1950, as the Army took players such as Buck Clayton and Illinois Jacquet came in.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: How long were you with the band altogether? From '39 to --

I left -- actually left about 1950, I would say about ten years. Of course, if you're speaking of the years like down in Little Rock and a couple of times like that, I would say 11 or 12, you know, in and out, you know, but about --
And the band changed a lot during that period.

Yeah, it did, it -- you know, well, I would say, you know, the Army carried some people out that didn't come back. Now, like Buck didn't -- when he went in the Army in '43, he didn't ever come back. I believe it was '43 Buck went in the Army. He never did return,
Yeah, Illinois was -- Illinois went over very good in that band. He really did. I liked him in that band. I think he played much more than he later did when he was in the band. People love him.
